title: Model Output Liability and Prompt Data Use Addendum - Draft
content:
Purpose and summary:
This attachment is intended to be appended to customer contracts (Master Services Agreement or DPA) where the supplier (Redwood Inference) provides hosted or dedicated inference services that may generate model outputs derived from customer-supplied prompts, data, or other inputs. Focus: allocate risk for harms arising from model outputs, clarify permitted uses of prompt and telemetry data for service operation and model improvement, and set controls and limitations for any reuse of customer prompts or outputs in training.

Key definitions (working):
- "Customer Input": any prompts, files, or parameters submitted by Customer to Redwood for inference.
- "Model Output": text, embeddings, classifications, or other artifacts returned by the service.
- "Improvement Use": any use of Customer Input/Model Output to evaluate, train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve models, features, or monitoring systems.

Negotiation notes (internal):
- Customers often ask to prohibit Improvement Use entirely. We should offer a narrow carve: allow Improvement Use on de-identified/aggregated telemetry with opt-out for enterprise customers (via contract line item).
- Consider additional fee-based option for customers who require absolute non-use for model improvement.

Core clauses (draft language):
1) Ownership and license of inputs/outputs:
   - Customer retains ownership of Customer Input. Redwood retains ownership of pre-existing models and model updates it creates.
   - Redwood grants Customer a non-exclusive license to Model Output for the Customer's internal business purposes.
   - Customer grants Redwood a limited license to use Customer Input and derived Model Output solely for service delivery, debugging, security, compliance, and (subject to Section 3) Improvement Use.

2) Use restrictions and export controls:
   - Customer will not submit Export-Controlled Data or data prohibited by law. Parties to add export clauses mirroring MSA export language.

3) Improvement Use and prompt data handling:
   - Default: Redwood may use Customer Input and non-personally-identifiable Model Output for service operation, telemetry, and aggregated quality analytics.
   - Improvement Use (model training or tuning) is permitted only in aggregated, de-identified form, and not for training models that will be sold to third parties, unless Customer provides explicit opt-in.
   - For Customers purchasing a "No-Model-Use" add-on, Redwood will not use Customer Input or associated Model Output for any Improvement Use. This will be a contract-priced option and may require Customer to assume higher operational risk and additional SLAs.

4) Prompt/Output retention and deletion:
   - Retention windows default to 90 days for raw Customer Input and 365 days for aggregated telemetry, unless otherwise agreed.
   - On Customer request (and subject to lawful restrictions), Redwood will attempt to delete Customer Input from active systems within 30 days; residual backups may persist for up to 90 days.

5) Risk allocation and liability for Model Outputs:
   - Redwood does not warrant that Model Output is accurate, complete, or fit for a particular purpose except as set out in a separate SLA.
   - Redwood's liability for claims arising solely from Model Output (e.g., hallucinations, incorrect factual statements) is limited to direct damages capped at the greater of USD 1,000,000 or the amounts paid by Customer under the applicable subscription in the preceding 12 months.
   - Exclusions: liability cap does not apply to gross negligence, willful misconduct, or violations of data protection obligations where Redwood is the controller for certain personal data.

6) Indemnities:
   - Customer indemnifies Redwood for claims arising from Customer's use of Model Output for unlawful activities or where Customer knowingly submits prohibited content.
   - Redwood indemnifies Customer for third-party IP claims to the extent that: (a) claim arises from Redwood's proprietary model weights, and (b) Customer's use complies with the Agreement and this Addendum.

7) Subprocessors and access controls:
   - Redwood will maintain a list of subprocessors with explanations for access purposes. For any subprocessor that has the ability to access decrypted Customer Input (e.g., for managed private deployments or on-prem support), Redwood will require contractual obligations mirroring customer commitments in this Addendum.
   - Remote access for troubleshooting must be authorized via ticket and logged; Customer may require MFA and allow-listing of IPs for support sessions.

8) Audit and compliance:
   - Customers on enterprise plans may request a security-focused audit of logging and retention procedures once per 12 months with 60 days notice; reasonable redaction permitted.

9) Incident handling and output-related harms:
   - If Redwood becomes aware of a systemic model failure causing material customer harm (e.g., disclosure of sensitive data via model output), Redwood will: notify Customer within 72 hours, provide a remediation plan, and offer mitigation support (e.g., model rollback, prompt-blocking rules).

10) Negotiation points for Legal/Prod teams:
   - Cap sizing: consider SLA tier attachment to materially increase cap for higher-priced tiers.
   - Opt-out flow: add contract language and UI/operational checklist to ensure opt-out for Improvement Use is enforced across training pipelines.
   - For private/on-prem deployments, default to "no Improvement Use" unless explicit consent is given; document how telemetry is collected in those environments.

Appendix A: Operational checklist (for Solutions Eng + SRE)
- Implement flagging: per-customer "no-model-use" boolean in telemetry pipeline.
- Logs: store support session transcripts encrypted and notify customer on any access.
- Retention flow: automated deletion job + manual escalation if deletion fails.

Appendix B: Suggested UI copy for customer-facing opt-in/out
- "Allow Redwood to use your anonymized prompts to improve models and service quality. You may opt out; opting out may result in reduced personalization and slower improvements."

Open questions / items for counsel:
- How to treat derivative model weights created after exposure to Customer Input (record-keeping on provenance).
- Required language for regulators in certain EU member states re: automated decision-making and liability.

Links / references (internal):
- Confluence: Model Governance Playbook (linked above)
- Security PR: github.com/redwood-inference/security/telemetry-redaction (WIP)
- Jira: JIRA-1234 (opt-out feature work)
notes: Working draft for legal review and product alignment. Prioritize enterprise use-cases where customers demand non-use. Include pricing attach for No-Model-Use option.
